steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper on offloading and quality control for AI-generated content (AIGC) services in 6G mobile edge computing networks, covering background, the challenges, related work, and our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- GAI and AIGC services
- Edge computing and its convergence with AIGC
- 6G and edge computing
- Why diffusion models are hard to deploy on devices
- Challenges
- Related work
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- GAI / AIGC
  - GPT models in spotlight; GAI transformative field in ML/AI, changed how people interact with digital world
  - AIGC = demonstration of GAI model capabilities
  - multiple AIGC models (e.g., diffusion) -> diverse outputs: text-to-speech, text-to-image, image-to-image
  - AIGC-as-a-Service (AaaS): generate content, repair corrupted images, alter input images -> immersive services for Metaverse users
- Edge computing
  - solves latency concerns of cloud computing; improves security + quality of networks via AI, Blockchain, digital twin
  - AIGC + edge computing = future research focus, esp. Metaverse (immersion of users)
- 6G
  - successor of 5G; improve reliability, speed, security far beyond 5G
  - 6G + edge computing: seamless, ultra-reliable, low-latency communication + powerful localized computing
  - enables apps needing high data rates, massive connectivity, ultra-reliable low latency -> eMBB, URLLC, mMTC
- Deployment problem
  - generic diffusion models (DALL-E 2, Imagen) need substantial memory; large parameter volume -> hard for real-time apps and constrained devices
  - lightweight models (text-to-image, 860M UNet + 123M text encoder) on consumer mobile devices -> quality inevitably affected
  - diffusion models + edge computing = important future direction
- Challenges
  - 1: only lightweight models locally -> lower quality; edge server hosts larger models but can't handle all tasks while generating high quality -> offloading decisions + quality level
  - 2: different processing locations -> different computation time; diverse, stringent latency needs -> tradeoff offloading vs computation time
  - 3: quality evaluation subjective -> need mathematical correlation between quality levels and diffusion models
- Related work
  - multiple surveys of diffusion models
  - diffusion steps vs image quality: forward diffusion dynamics, smaller diffusion times to bridge ideal vs simulated
  - number of reverse diffusion steps as variable; optimal step balancing image quality vs diffusion time
  - AIGC + edge: diffusion-based AI-generated optimal decision (AGOD) algorithm for selecting AIGC service providers (AGPs)
  - ours: resource allocation for AGOD; correlate image quality to diffusion steps; consider computation time and utility
- Contributions
  - first resource allocation for diffusion models in edge computing with guaranteed AIGC quality; better system performance and user experience
  - quantify AIGC quality via reverse diffusion steps + average error of computation results
  - optimization algorithm jointly optimizes tradeoff between offloading decisions and utility of AIGC models

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
With GPT models in the spotlight, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI), a transformative field inside the wider landscape of machine learning and artificial intelligence, has changed how people interact with and understand the digital world. When Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) models demonstrate their capabilities, this is called AI-generated content (AIGC). As AIGC techniques develop, several AIGC models (e.g., diffusion models) can be used to generate outputs in diverse forms, including text-to-speech, text-to-image, and image-to-image. So the AIGC-as-a-Service (AaaS) architecture is proposed to offer generated content, repair corrupted images, or alter input images, which gives Metaverse users immersive AIGC services.

Edge computing is a new computing paradigm. It solves the latency concerns of cloud computing, and it also improves the security and quality of the communication networks by integrating with other key technologies including AI, Blockchain, and digital twin. Combining AIGC models with the edge computing paradigm is becoming the focus of future research, especially in the Metaverse field, which emphasizes user immersion.

6G is the successor of the current 5G wireless communication network, and it aims to improve reliability, speed, and security further, far beyond what 5G can do. Integrating 6G with edge computing is expected to revolutionize network architectures and computing, giving seamless, ultra-reliable, low-latency communication together with powerful, localized computing. This will enable new applications and services that need high data rates, massive connectivity, and ultra-reliable low-latency communications, resulting in enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), and massive machine type communications (mMTC).

- deployment problem: generic diffusion models (DALL-E 2, Imagen) need lots of memory, large parameter volume -> hard for real-time / constrained devices; lightweight model (860M UNet, 123M text encoder) on mobile -> lower quality; diffusion + edge important direction
- Challenges: (1) offloading decisions + quality level; (2) offloading vs computation time under latency requirements; (3) mathematical correlation between quality levels and diffusion models
- Related work: surveys; forward diffusion dynamics with smaller diffusion times; reverse diffusion steps as variable to balance quality vs time; AGOD algorithm for selecting AGPs; ours: resource allocation for AGOD with quality-steps correlation, computation time, utility
- Contributions: 3 bullets

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
With GPT models in the spotlight, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI), a transformative field inside the wider landscape of machine learning and artificial intelligence, has changed how people interact with and understand the digital world. When Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) models demonstrate their capabilities, this is called AI-generated content (AIGC). As AIGC techniques develop, several AIGC models (e.g., diffusion models) can be used to generate outputs in diverse forms, including text-to-speech, text-to-image, and image-to-image. So the AIGC-as-a-Service (AaaS) architecture is proposed to offer generated content, repair corrupted images, or alter input images, which gives Metaverse users immersive AIGC services.

Edge computing is a new computing paradigm. It solves the latency concerns of cloud computing, and it also improves the security and quality of the communication networks by integrating with other key technologies including AI, Blockchain, and digital twin. Combining AIGC models with the edge computing paradigm is becoming the focus of future research, especially in the Metaverse field, which emphasizes user immersion.

6G is the successor of the current 5G wireless communication network, and it aims to improve reliability, speed, and security further, far beyond what 5G can do. Integrating 6G with edge computing is expected to revolutionize network architectures and computing, giving seamless, ultra-reliable, low-latency communication together with powerful, localized computing. This will enable new applications and services that need high data rates, massive connectivity, and ultra-reliable low-latency communications, resulting in enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), and massive machine type communications (mMTC).

However, generic diffusion models (e.g., Open AI's DALL-E 2 and Google's Imagen) need substantial memory storage, and deploying large AIGC models is hard because of their large number of parameters, which is an obstacle for real-time applications and for devices with limited computational resources. Lightweight diffusion models (like the text-to-image model with an 860M UNet and a 123M text encoder proposed in prior work) are used on consumer mobile devices, but the quality of the generated content will inevitably be affected. So combining diffusion models with edge computing systems has become an important direction for future research.

Challenges: Mobile devices have limited resources, so only lightweight diffusion models can be deployed locally, and the content generated locally usually has a lower quality level. Larger models can be deployed on the edge server, but the server still can't handle all the computational tasks at the same time while generating high-quality content. So the first challenge is the offloading decisions and the quality level of the generated content. Second, processing the computational task in different locations means the computation time is always different. Mobile users have diverse and stringent latency requirements, so how to balance the tradeoff between offloading decisions and computation time is the second challenge. Also, evaluating the quality level of generated content is subjective, so we need to establish a mathematical correlation between quality levels and diffusion models, which is the third challenge.

Related Work: Recently, many studies have reviewed the state-of-the-art research and development in diffusion models. On diffusion steps and image quality, one work focuses on the forward diffusion dynamics and uses smaller diffusion times to bridge the gap between the ideal and the simulated. Another work treats the number of reverse diffusion steps as a variable and finds the optimal reverse diffusion step to balance the tradeoff between image quality and diffusion time. For combining AIGC models with edge computing, another work introduces the diffusion model-based AI-generated optimal decision (AGOD) algorithm, which gives the optimal strategy for selecting AIGC service providers (AGPs). Different from these works, we propose a resource allocation scheme for the AGOD that correlates image quality with the diffusion steps and takes the computation time and the utility of AIGC models into account.

Contributions: The main contributions of this work are:

- We are the first to implement resource allocation for diffusion models in edge computing systems while guaranteeing the quality of the AIGC, which can improve the performance of the system and the experience of users.

- We quantify the quality level of AIGC by considering the reverse diffusion steps in the diffusion process and also the average error of computation results.

- Our optimization algorithm jointly optimizes the tradeoff between the offloading decisions of the computational tasks and the utility of AIGC models.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
With GPT models capturing the spotlight, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI), as a transformative field within the broader landscape of machine learning and artificial intelligence, has changed the way people interact with and understand the digital world [1]. The demonstration of the capabilities of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) models is referred to as AI-generated content (AIGC). With the development of AIGC techniques, multiple AIGC models (e.g., diffusion models) can be employed to generate outputs in diverse forms, including text-to-speech, text-to-image, and image-to-image [2]. Therefore, the AIGC-as-a-Service (AaaS) architecture is proposed to offer generated content, repair corrupted images, or alter inputted images, providing Metaverse users with immersive AIGC services.

Edge computing, as a novel computing paradigm, not only solves the latency concerns of cloud computing but also improves the security and quality of the communication networks involved by integrating with other key technologies including AI, Blockchain, and digital twin [3]. The convergence of AIGC models and the edge computing paradigm is becoming the focus of future research, especially in the Metaverse field [4], which emphasizes the immersion of users.

6G, as the successor of the current 5G wireless communication network, aims to make further improvements in reliability, speed, and security, far surpassing the capabilities of 5G. The integration of 6G with edge computing is expected to revolutionize network architectures and computing, offering seamless, ultra-reliable, low-latency communication coupled with powerful, localized computing capabilities. This convergence will enable new applications and services that require high data rates, massive connectivity, and ultra-reliable low-latency communications, resulting in enhanced mobile broadband (eMBB), ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC), and massive machine type communications (mMTC).

Nonetheless, generic diffusion models (e.g., Open AI's DALL-E 2 [5] and Google's Imagen [6]) require substantial memory storage, and deploying large AIGC models is challenging due to the large volume of parameters [7], which creates obstacles for real-time applications and devices with constrained computational resources. Though lightweight diffusion models (like the text-to-image model with 860M UNet and 123M text encoder proposed in [8]) are employed on consumer mobile devices, the quality of generated content will inevitably be affected. Thus, the convergence of diffusion models and edge computing systems has become an important direction for future research.

Challenges: Given the resource constraints of mobile devices, only lightweight diffusion models can be deployed on local devices, so locally generated content typically exhibits a lower quality level. While larger models can be deployed on the edge server, it cannot simultaneously manage all computational tasks while generating high-quality content. Consequently, the first challenge centers on the offloading decisions and the quality level of the generated content. Secondly, processing the computational task in different locations means the computation time is always different. As mobile users have diverse and stringent latency requirements, how to balance the tradeoff between the offloading decisions and computation time is the second challenge. Furthermore, the subjective nature of evaluating the quality level of generated content requires establishing a mathematical correlation between quality levels and diffusion models, which constitutes the third challenge.

Related Work: Recently, multiple studies have reviewed the state-of-the-art research and development in diffusion models [9,10,11,12,13,14]. Notably, in research on diffusion steps and image quality, [13] focuses on the forward diffusion dynamics to bridge the gap between the ideal and the simulated by adopting smaller diffusion times. Furthermore, [15] treats the number of reverse diffusion steps as a variable to find the optimal reverse diffusion step that balances the tradeoff between image quality and diffusion time. For the convergence of AIGC models and the edge computing paradigm, [16] introduces the diffusion model-based AI-generated optimal decision (AGOD) algorithm to provide the optimal strategy for selecting AIGC service providers (AGPs). Unlike these previous works, we propose a resource allocation scheme for the AGOD by correlating image quality to the diffusion steps and taking the computation time and utility of AIGC models into consideration.

Contributions: The main contributions of this work are:

- • We pioneer the implementation of resource allocation for diffusion models in edge computing systems while guaranteeing the quality of the AIGC, which could enhance the performance of the system and the experience of users respectively.

- • We quantify the quality level of AIGC by taking the reverse diffusion steps within the diffusion process into consideration, together with the average error of computation results.

- • The proposed optimization algorithm jointly optimizes the tradeoff between the offloading decisions of the computational tasks and the utility of AIGC models.
